extra.message: User-controlled req.body.login (POST /app/usersearch) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string 'SELECT name,id FROM Users WHERE login="+req.body.login+"' passed to db.sequelize.query(). An attacker can break out of the string literal (e.g. ' OR '1'='1) to read/modify arbitrary rows, bypass auth, or extract data.

User-controlled req.body.address (POST /app/ping) is concatenated into the shell command 'ping -c 2 ' and executed via child_process.exec(). Input like '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd' (or with backticks/$(...)) yields arbitrary OS command execution as the server user.

Uploaded file bytes are passed directly to node-serialize unserialize() (POST /app/bulkproductslegacy). node-serialize 0.0.4 executes JavaScript embedded in serialized objects (known gadget: {"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){...}()"}), giving unauthenticated-style RCE from a crafted file upload. Use JSON.parse instead.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: libxmljs.parseXmlString() is called on attacker-controlled uploaded XML with noent:true, which enables entity substitution. A crafted <!DOCTYPE> with an external entity can read arbitrary local files (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) or trigger SSRF against internal hosts, and results are persisted into product fields.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: userEditSubmit (POST /app/useredit) looks up the user by attacker-supplied req.body.id (hidden form field 'id', views/app/useredit.ejs:28) with no check that it equals req.user.id. Any authenticated user can set another user's id and overwrite that victim's name, email, and password (bCrypt hash at line 153), enabling account takeover of any account.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /app/admin/usersapi is an admin function but only requires authHandler.isAuthenticated - there is no req.user.role=='admin' check (compare /app/admin UI gate in views/app/admin.ejs). Any logged-in non-admin user can call it and dump every user record, defeating the admin-only access control.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: listUsersAPI returns all User rows (via db.User.findAll({})) as JSON, including the bcrypt password hash, email, login and role of every user. Combined with the missing admin check on /app/admin/usersapi, any authenticated user can harvest password hashes for offline cracking and expose PII.

The password-reset token is computed as md5(req.query.login) (line 49; re-checked at line 78 in resetPwSubmit). It is deterministic and requires no secret, so an attacker who knows a victim's login can trivially compute md5(login), pass GET /resetpw?login=<user>&token=<md5>, and set a new password for that account - full account takeover. A cryptographically random, expiring token is required.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: GET /app/redirect (routes/app.js:48, no auth) redirects to the unvalidated req.query.url. An attacker can craft a link to /app/redirect?url=https://evil.example to phish users, and because it sits on a trusted origin it also passes common 'redirect' allowlist/SSO checks.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Reflected XSS: req.body.name from productSearch (core/appHandler.js:68) is stored in output.searchTerm and emitted with the unescaped EJS tag <%- output.searchTerm %>. A crafted search query such as <script>alert(document.cookie)</script> executes in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: Stored XSS: product name/code/tags/description saved from req.body in modifyProductSubmit (core/appHandler.js:115-118) or bulk imports are rendered unescaped via <%- output.products[i].name %> etc. on the product listing page. Any user who can add/edit a product can inject script that runs for every visitor to /app/products.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: DOM-based XSS: user-controlled fields returned by GET /app/admin/usersapi (name/email, set by any user via /app/useredit) are written with c_id/c_name/c_email.innerHTML = users[i]...., so markup in a stored name/email executes in the (admin) victim's browser when the admin page loads. Use textContent.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: All state-changing routes (usersearch, ping, products, modifyproduct, useredit, calc, bulkproducts*) are plain POST handlers with no CSRF token, and the csurf dependency in package.json is never wired up in server.js. Combined with the default session cookie (no SameSite), a cross-site form/request can perform actions as the victim (e.g. change password via /app/useredit).

express-session cookie is configured with secure:false and no httpOnly/SameSite options, and the app listens on 0.0.0.0 (config/server.js:2) without TLS. Session IDs are transmitted in cleartext and readable by client script, enabling session hijacking over the network.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The express-session signing secret is the hardcoded, publicly-known value 'keyboard cat'. An attacker who knows the secret can forge/authenticate arbitrary session cookies, defeating session integrity. The secret should come from a protected environment variable.
